title: What is a fair price?
review: What constitutes a fair price when you are looking to sell a Rolex on the grey market?   I spotted a SkyDweller on BQ Watches' website and decided to try to sell them my 2007 SS white dial Daytona (excellent condition w/ box & papers, case and bracelet recently professionally polished ) in exchange. After being cut off twice, I called them for the third time and was offered £12,000. Daytonas of similar vintage on their site are on offer for £20 - 22k.  Had I sold it, I am confident they would be asking £20 - 22k (perhaps more.)   So a gross profit of £8 - 10k (£8k = 67%  profit, £10k = 83% profit.)  Seems a bit on the high side to me.  Actually, very much on the high side, but then I've very limited experience selling.  Perhaps the take-away is that if you're new to selling on the grey market you need to drastically lower your expectations!  Fair or not, my Daytona is not going anywhere for £12k.

title: Not happy enough to keep the product
review: I purchased 2 of the Fire 10 tablets but on review I am not happy with them.  I was aware that the OS was not fully Android and that not all apps would be available,  For me two of those that I use regularly fell into this category.  Lee mentioned a phone help line and said "more on this later" but never mentioned it again.  I do use the Kindle app but was disappointed to see the the page turning on my tablet was just a slide across whereas on the demo it showed a proper page turning graphic.    I have no idea how to access my library as that is now not part of the menu and I don't find moving around the various menus is intuitive.   All seems designed to get you to purchase more goods from Amazon.  The bottom line is that the tablet is no better than what I already have and I will be returning both tablets.

title: Putting the Coyote III to the test
review: We purchased the Oex Coyote III 3-person tent as a roomier two-person tent, and used it for the first time this week for six consecutive nights. It stayed waterproof except for the base of the sleeping compartment which got slightly damp. The real test was the final night of camping with winds in the 30s (mph) and gusts up to 44 mph. Twice the wind forced open the zippers on the vestibule entrances, and the guy ropes quickly became slack and had to be re-tightened several times during the night. When we took the tent down, we discovered that most of the metal pegs had started to corrode (after just six days) which was disappointing. The alloy poles, however, definitely held their own in the wind. Overall, the Coyote III tent did quite well, and we now know its limits with wind (nothing more than 30 mph). It was a good purchase for £150 and we plan to get a lot of use out of it, albeit in fairer weather.

title: Gift cards are not good
review: Great shop. Quality gear. Informative staff. Just bought new boots for dog walks. Let down by the gift card I had being past the year use date. I strongly disagree with gift cards running out of time. The company has the money it is not ok in my opinion to then keep that but not honour it. I don't believe there should be a time limit but if there is then I think the money should be refunded. Not ok just to take my £50 birthday gift!

title: shipped me a faulty EVOC backpack
review: shipped me a faulty EVOC backpack, customer service not great - missing a part of the waist buckle. email address for customer service not getting thru, so I called next day. Got a different email address, still awaiting reply. I do want the EVOC backpack, so hoped Tiso would be able to send the missing part. Looks like a return/refund coming up....

title: Lost / delayed delivery and poor customer service
review: I ordered a roof tent which got lost in transit and seemed to be returned by the courier to Tiso. I called Tiso for updates and whilst staff were friendly when I called, I didn’t feel confident or assured that the item would actually ever arrive. Eventually I was notified, with barely more than 90 mins notice, of a delivery slot. Far from ideal during working hours and it was only by luck that someone was available to receive the delivery at that time.

title: Poor refund experience
review: I had to return something to your company for a refund. I attended your store in Edinburgh and more than 7 days later I am still waiting for a refund back to my account. Very poor given you commit to a five day turn around.

title: Ordered online
review: Ordered online, seemed to take ages to arrive, compared to Cotswold Outdoor who  always have automatically delivered next day.  Swimming goggles great, had the security tag not been left on the nose bridge.  Facing a 60 mile round trip to get it taken off was not an option.  Had to borrow some cutters from a neighbour and an annoyance at the oversight from the shop.

title: Time taken to deliver goods
review: Time taken to deliver goods, very poor. Ordered items from Amazon later the same day I placed order with Tiso, Amazon arrived within 24 hours, Tiso took over 6 days!Received updates about delivery from Tiso and DPD which were confusing and unhelpful.

title: Ordered a bike
review: Ordered a bike, 11 days after despatch it went “missing” at the couriers. Tiso customer services did sort me a refund out, which came through two weeks after the initial purchase.The whole experience was hassle. Tiso customer services were decent though.It’s a shame about the couriers.

title: I bought a pair of Scarpa Ranger Activ…
review: I bought a pair of Scarpa Ranger Activ boots about a year ago and this summer they started to leak. Tiso sent the boots away for testing and announced they were completely waterproof. However, they are still leaking. I am an experienced hillwalker so am well aware of how to look after boots. Furthermore, Tiso appear to be reluctant to post my two-star review on their website. Such a shame as I have always had a good experience with Tiso in the past.
